text:
Tomasz Okonjo has won this year's Calder Vane Prize for architecture, the prize's jury announced on 14 March at its annual ceremony in Veldmark Hall.

Ilse Marchetti-Brandt, chair of the jury, delivered the announcement. The decision is set out in the jury's published citation, "Statement of the 2025 Architecture Jury," which was read aloud to the assembled guests during the evening.

The award carries a purse of 250,000 credits.

According to the published statement, the jury reached its choice after considering the full field of candidates for the year. Ms Marchetti-Brandt presented the citation as the panel's formal account of its reasoning, and the document remains the authoritative record of the decision.

Mr Okonjo's win was confirmed in the text of the statement and in the chair's remarks from the podium. The Calder Vane Prize is presented once a year, and the architecture award is announced at the same ceremony as the prize's other honours.
